subject: Enterprise onboarding: access origination plan and access ownership
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@cedarbrook.com>, Tom Evans <tevans@cedarbrook.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Enterprise onboarding: access origination plan and access ownership

Hi Rachel / Tom —

Thanks for the time on Tuesday. Per our kickoff, I wanted to capture the high-level access plan so we have clear owners and a short roadmap for the next two weeks. Key areas we need to confirm:

- SSO / SAML metadata exchange (IdP metadata, ACS/EntityIDs)
- SCIM provisioning mapping (users / groups / attributes)
- IP allowlist and CIDR ranges for staging + prod
- Dedicated service accounts for automated syncs and job runners
- Org policies: who manages role mappings and admin entitlements post-cutover

Owners suggested: Redwood (Monica) for SCIM mapping support and service-account perms; Redwood (Ben) for network egress allowlist and routing tests; Cedarbrook (Tom) for IdP metadata and internal approvers. Sean (me) will coordinate cutover windows and our fallback plan.

Deliverables this week we need from Cedarbrook: IdP metadata file, SCIM attribute examples, and the list of IPs for your egress / proxy. I attached a SCIM mapping template and a sample service-account permissions spreadsheet to get started.

Proposed milestone dates:
- 3/10: Exchange SAML metadata + complete SCIM mapping draft
- 3/12: Network allowlist confirmed and smoke test plan agreed
- 3/16: Staging cutover window (2 hours)

Can you confirm these owners and the 3/10 milestone? If that works I’ll open a short MRP (mutual action plan) ticket in the tracker and loop in your security approver.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: cedarbrook_scim_mapping.csv (csv), service-account-perms.xlsx (xlsx), sso-saml-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@cedarbrook.com>

Cc: Tom Evans <tevans@cedarbrook.com>, Cedarbrook IT <it@cedarbrook.com>

Subject: Re: Enterprise onboarding: access origination plan and access ownership

Sean —

Thanks for laying this out. 3/10 for the SAML metadata and SCIM draft is tight but doable. I’ll be the primary Cedarbrook contact for approvals and I’ve asked Tom to pull our IdP metadata and a sample user CSV. Expect the following by EOD 3/9:

- IdP metadata XML (Tom)
- SCIM sample attributes and current provisioning rules (Cedarbrook IT)
- Initial list of allowed egress IPs (security team) — note we need to validate with our corporate proxy; I’ll flag any ranges that require procurement tickets.

One ask: for service accounts, can you send the minimal IAM perms you need? We prefer to scope least privilege up front.

I’ll confirm owners once Tom validates the timing.

—Rachel
Senior Program Manager, Integrations
Cedarbrook Financial

Date: 2026-03-09T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise onboarding: access origination plan and access ownership

Hi all —

Thanks Rachel — I’ll take point on the SCIM mapping and service-account permissions. To make procurement/least-privilege reviews faster, I’ve attached a one-page perms matrix and a recommended RBAC mapping for typical Cedarbrook roles (admin, app-integrator, read-only). To answer your ask, Tom: the service accounts Redwood needs for the initial rollout are:

1) scim-sync@redwood (used by our provisioning worker) — needs: create/read/update/delete users, read groups, update group membership
2) logs-upload@redwood (optional for audit shipping) — needs: write-only to your designated ingest bucket / endpoint
3) job-runner@redwood (for scheduled inference jobs in staging) — needs: run/execute on the staging project, read-only on secrets store

We intentionally separate scim-sync from job-runner so you can lock down user lifecycle from compute jobs. Please confirm if Cedarbrook requires explicit scoped delegation (yes/no) and whether your proxy will NAT outgoing traffic; we’ll use that for the allowlist tests.

I’ve also pasted a short smoke-test plan below we intend to run during the 3/16 staging window:
- Validate SAML auth redirect with one test user (saml assertion payload check)
- Provision user via SCIM create and confirm group membership sync
- Job-runner execution with service-account token to confirm role scope
- Verify audit logs delivered to your ingest endpoint (if enabled)

If we get the SAML metadata + SCIM sample by 3/9 EOD we’ll prepare the staging app and share a test checklist by 3/11.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: service-account-perms.xlsx (xlsx), sso-saml-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@cedarbrook.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Tom Evans <tevans@cedarbrook.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Enterprise onboarding: access origination plan and access ownership

Rachel / Tom —

Quick operational notes ahead of the SAML exchange tomorrow:

1) IP allowlist: we tested our egress set for staging and prod. For staging please allow the following CIDRs: 54.183.12.0/24, 54.183.13.0/24. For prod (once you sign-off) we’ll provide the exact ranges but expect +/– same /22 block. If your proxy NATs, please confirm the external egress IP(s) so we can whitelist the right entry.

2) Time sync and certs: Ensure your IdP cert validity window extends past the anticipated cutover (>= 30 days). If your team rotates certs automatically, let us know the rotation cadence so we can avoid interruptions.

3) Rollback plan (short): if any SAML assertions fail during staging, we’ll pause and pivot to manual-provisioned accounts for affected users; SCIM changes are reversible but we’ll snapshot the user list before the cutover.

Action items for Cedarbrook (by 3/10 EOD):
- Upload IdP metadata XML to the shared tracker link (or email directly to me)
- Confirm whether your proxy NATs outgoing connections (Yes/No)
- Confirm scim-sync account acceptance of the perms matrix

I’ll kick off a brief runbook in the tracker with the staging test checklist and tentative 3/16 window. Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth cutover.

—Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Forwarded message included above.
